report.clinical_summary: The patient has HIV and is on Dovato (dolutegravir + lamivudine), having transitioned from a different medication about 5 months ago. They report feeling 'a bit down' and experiencing sleep changes (longer to fall asleep, more frequent nighttime waking) and reduced energy. They have occasional vivid dreams as a side effect. Their viral load is trending down but not yet undetectable. They have good adherence to the daily one-tablet regimen. They view HIV as a lifelong condition that is part of their identity, and they feel they have significant control over their health through proactive management. They experience challenges in romantic relationships due to HIV disclosure and some days feel overwhelmed emotionally, but generally maintain activities and connections. They have concerns about long-term medication effects (hormonal imbalances) and whether they'll ever be able to stop taking medication.

evidence.quote: HIV has certainly impacted my life in many ways. I think the most noticeable change has been in my relationships — especially romantic ones. It's a challenging topic to bring up when getting to know someone new, and there are times when people have reacted negatively or with discomfort.
In terms of mood and activities, I will admit that there are days when the weight of everything feels overwhelming.

consequences.reasoning: The patient has experienced significant changes in romantic relationships due to HIV disclosure and negative reactions. They report days when the 'weight of everything feels overwhelming.' However, they still enjoy hobbies and maintain connections with friends and family. This suggests a major role (romantic relationships) has been affected, but other aspects of life continue.
